content: I’ll document here some feedback from adapting the Kourovka paper repository to make it compliant with the Palomar Registry.

1. Maybe clarify metadata for repositories with several results

One Palomar submission describes one Comparator result, but a root formalization.yaml may (it is actually supposed to IIRC) describe an entire repository. In my case, the repository contains 9 results from different areas / sub-areas, so one classification cannot accurately describe both the repository and Problem 18.50.

I kept the root file repository-wide and used Palomar/Problem_18_50/formalization.yaml for the submission.

Maybe we should document this as the recommended layout for multi-result repositories. What do you think?

2. Maybe add fields for editors and "problem proposers"

A project solving one or more open problems might need other fields like:

  • "problem proposer" (e.g. Erdos & Nathanson, etc.).
  • "editors" (if it's a collection like the Kourovka notebook or erdosproblems.com by @Thomas Bloom).
  • "solution / paper authors".

The schema records only source authors, so I had to list the Kourovka Notebook editors as authors and mention the proposer in notes.

For multi-result repos from different areas, maybe the solution is to have classification fields for each result rather than for the entire repository... these can be optional, but there can be some sort of "wildcard" repo-wide classification field that then makes the result-wise fields mandatory. I don't know if multiple formalization.yaml files is necessarily the best layout as that might make the repository harder to read... but I also don't see great alternatives...
Yes, it is exactly what I am doing https://github.com/pitmonticone/Kourovka/pull/2.

No, I meant on the level of the formalization.yaml file design - so that there can be a single repo-wide formalization.yaml, where for each declaration, there can be a different subject classification. Eg.

  - declaration: "kourovka_18_50"
    file: "Kourovka/Problem_18_50.lean"
    sorry_count: 0
    axioms: ["propext", "Classical.choice", "Quot.sound"]
    classification:
    - arxiv: ["math.GR", "math.CO"]
      msc2020: ["20E25", "20E22", "20D60", "17B38", "20B30", "05C25", "20F60", "20D15"]

What do you think?
But I also need to provide all the other problem- and declaration-specific information and I’m worried it could quickly become quite messy.

I think the solution in the PR above is simple and scalable enough to be adopted as the standard for now, if the maintainers agree.

Unfortunately, I won’t have much availability to discuss it further, so I’ll check the maintainers’ decision over the weekend and follow whatever approach they settle on.

Thanks!

I've made some small changes in how we handle repositories with multiple comparator configs.

However there is a fundamental tension here: formalization.yaml is meant to describe the whole repository, yet Palomar is trying to index an arbitrary subset (possible multiple subsets), as described by the comparator config.

  1. We're just going to say that this situation (a large repository, and compator config(s) pointing at a subset) are mildly discouraged, and simply not going to be as well supported as a repository with a single headline result.
  2. Nevertheless we'll try to support it. My preference is to try to use a global formalization.yaml, but if it is not possible to reconcile that with Palomar's needs then to fall back to multiple formalization.yamls and specify the path in the submission form.

(I think Sid's suggestion to have per-declaration classifications is too complicated.)

Pietro Monticone said:

  1. Maybe add fields for editors and "problem proposers"

This is now supported (and documented):

  sources:
    - title: "..."
      authors:
        - "Bibliographic author"
      contributors:
        - name: "Pietro"
          role: "problem proposer"

There's also a formalization.yaml PR updating the schema.
